title: Our Home
description:
For the first time since getting engaged, they browsed Gangnam listings together.

Scrolling past a three-bedroom, Daeun's hand stopped.
"This room... how about it for your father?"
{name} froze. He'd never even thought of it.
"And this side, for when my mom comes up to Seoul."

The three billion that had been 'my deed' for five years became something else with that one sentence.
A number he'd climbed alone — was now a home with several rooms.

choices.text: "Yeah. Let's find one with a room for both of them."
choices.result_text:
Daeun beamed.

That night, for the first time, {name} thought of Gangnam not as 'where I arrive' but 'where we live.'
The weight of the number changed. Heavier now — and yet, strangely, lighter.

choices.text: "Let's think about that after we get in. Right now the number comes first."
choices.result_text:
Daeun went quiet for a moment, then closed the screen.
"...Right. The number comes first."

{name} felt the temperature of her voice drop half a degree, but his head was already back in the listing math.
How many rooms it had — was a problem for later.

description_if_known.father_passed:
For the first time since getting engaged, they browsed Gangnam listings together.

Scrolling past a three-bedroom, Daeun's hand stopped.
"Let's keep this room for your father. Hang a photo of him."
{name} froze. His father was gone now — but Daeun wanted to leave a place for him.

"And this side, for when my mom comes up to Seoul."

The three billion that had been 'my deed' for five years became something else.
A number he'd climbed alone — was now a home with a place for both the departed and the living.

title: The Families Meet
description:
The introductions. A quiet Korean restaurant.

{name}'s father — a lifetime in the factory, stooped shoulders, a borrowed suit. Daeun's mother — up on the dawn bus from the countryside, knuckles thick from work.

Neither of them had anything. You could see it at a glance.

His father spoke, with effort.
"I... once did a terrible thing to my child, over a debt. A shameful father..."

Silence settled over the table. Daeun's mother looked at {name}.
Whatever {name} said next — his father's remaining pride hung on it.

choices.text: "My father paid off every won of that debt. Everything I am, I owe to him."
choices.result_text:
His father lifted his head. His eyes were red.

Daeun's mother said quietly, "You've got a good father."

On the way home, his father clapped {name} once on the back.
No words — but that was enough.

choices.text: Change the subject. (The debt talk doesn't belong here)
choices.result_text:
{name} hurried to bring up something else. The venue, the date, the budget.

And so his father's words were buried, trailing off over the table.

On the way home, his father was quieter than usual.
{name} knew what that silence meant, and pretended he didn't.

title: The Shortcut
description:
The deadline was close. One step short of Gangnam.

Sangchul pushed a coffee across the table.
"There is one way. Take out a loan under your in-laws' name, hold the property under your wife's name — and you skip the taxes, the regulations, all of it."

"Your wife doesn't even need to know. Just get her stamp on the papers."

Using his wife as a name on a document. And Gangnam would be in reach.
Sangchul smiled. It was a smile he'd seen somewhere before.

choices.text: "Forget it. Daeun isn't a document."
choices.result_text:
Sangchul shrugged. "Well. Your call."

The road home was long. Gangnam drifted a step further away.
And yet, strangely, his steps were light.

{name} understood now why that smile was familiar. Five years ago, that's how someone had smiled while introducing a deal to his father.

choices.text: "...Just her stamp, right." (Borrows his wife's name)
choices.result_text:
Daeun stamped the papers without asking a thing. Because she trusts {name}.

The moment he turned that trust into a document, {name} became Sangchul.
Started out hating him, ended up doing that to his own wife.

Gangnam came a step closer. And something, soundlessly, cracked.

title: The Last Step
description:
One document remained, looking like the last shortcut to Gangnam.

Years ago, {name} had put the property under Daeun's name. If he turned the trust he borrowed then into permission to sell today, there would be no going back.

The contract lay before him. From the kitchen came the sound of a knife touching the cutting board.
"Minjun, is it okay if I put scallions in the rolled omelet?"

Daeun was asking about one small preference at dinner. {name} was about to decide the shape of her whole life without asking at all.

choices.text: Count the knife beats from the kitchen instead of reading the contract.
choices.result_text: The knife touched the board. One, two. The rhythm of an ordinary evening gathered over the signature line.

choices.text: Trace the name 'Kim Daeun' in the ownership field.
choices.result_text: Her name took one short line. The debt, collateral, and numbers beneath it ran much longer.

description_if_known.namsan_lock_daeun:

Years ago, {name} had put the property under Daeun's name. If he turned the trust he borrowed then into permission to sell today, there would be no going back.

As he reached for the pen, the lock on the Namsan railing came back to him. The night they had said they would find it in ten years. That lock would still be there.

From the kitchen came the sound of a knife on a cutting board.
"Minjun, is it okay if I put scallions in the rolled omelet?"

Daeun was asking about one small preference at dinner. {name} was about to decide the shape of her whole life without asking at all.

title: The Kitchen Rhythm
description:
Daeun had asked whether to add scallions because even a preference that small was not hers to decide for the person beside her.

Years ago, she had handed over her seal without asking why. She trusted {name}. That trust was not permission for today.

"Minjun?"
"Yeah. Put them in."

That answer was easy. Only the answer at the contract remained.

choices.text: Go back to the contract waiting on the table.
choices.result_text: The knife resumed its rhythm. {name} picked up the pen.

title: Her Name
description:
Kim Daeun. One short name held a dawn convenience store, rolled omelet, years of waiting, and the seal she had handed him in trust.

The document reduced all of that to a single ownership field. {name} had been reading people that way for a long time.

"Daeun."
"Yes?"
"...Nothing."

Her humming stopped for half a beat, then continued in the kitchen.

choices.text: Lift his finger from her name and pick up the pen.
choices.result_text: Only one thing remained: whether to sign.

title: The Last Step
description:
The pen stopped above the signature line.

Whether this paper would ever reach Gangnam was still for the numbers to decide. What it turned Daeun's trust into would be decided now.

The knife in the kitchen fell silent. {name} chose his final answer.

choices.text: Put the pen down. "Daeun, let's just... get there a little later."
choices.result_text:
Daeun came out of the kitchen. "What'd you say?"
"Nothing. The rolled omelet smells good."

The shortcut went in the trash that night.
Gangnam would come honestly, or it wouldn't come at all — one of the two.
Either way, he wasn't trading it for the person making dinner in the kitchen.
{name} learned that day it was worth more than any deed.

choices.text: Sign it. Trust the numbers one more time.
choices.result_text:
He signed. When he set the pen down, the page slowly settled flat against the desk.

It did not take Daeun long to learn the truth. A few days later, she spread a copy of the contract across the dining table. Dinner sat untouched and cold.

"...When did you start seeing me as paperwork?"

{name} opened his mouth, then closed it. He tried to choose a date, but first came all the nights he had postponed an answer and all the mornings he had calculated alone.

Daeun watched his face for a long time. Still, she did not cry. She looked like someone who had been crying in pieces for years, never enough at once for him to notice.

She took the seal she had reclaimed that day from the drawer and pressed it onto the last page of the agreement ending their life together.

The sound was short and dry. Softer than the knife stopping in the kitchen, and clear enough that nothing could be taken back.

choices.text: (Pen in hand — that post-it in the drawer came to mind.)
choices.result_text:
Pen still in hand, {name} opened the desk drawer.
One old post-it note. Years had passed since he peeled it off the fridge and put it here.
'Eat properly.' Three words, written careful and round.

The person who wrote those words was in the kitchen making rolled omelet. Selling off everything she had with one secret signature — and those three words — could not exist in the same world.

{name} stuck the post-it onto the contract, and put the pen down.
"Daeun. Let's just... go a little late."
The humming in the kitchen paused a moment, then went on. Knowing nothing. That was good.

title: The Wedding Package
description:
Wedding prep. {name} took the estimate in hand and, for a moment, couldn't breathe.

Studio-dress-makeup package: 4.8 million. Hall rental and catering: 18 million. Ye-dan and gifts: 5 million. Honeymoon: 4 million.
Five separate invitation dinners, each one on {name}'s tab.

All told, it was a jeonse deposit's worth. That much comes straight out of the seed money for Gangnam.

Daeun glanced at the estimate and said,
"...Do we really have to do it like this?"

choices.text: "Let's keep it small. Minimal package, put that money toward our home."
choices.result_text:
Daeun smiled, relieved.
"Honestly, spending millions to wear a dress for one day felt like a waste to me too."

A small hall, family and a few close friends. Self-shot photos by the Han River instead of a studio.
Cutting the guest list was harder than expected. They called the people they could not invite and sat through more than one wounded reply.

They finished the day with money left over and their closest faces around them. Some people, however, would never share that one photograph.

choices.text: "It's once in a lifetime. Let's do it like everyone else does."
choices.result_text:
They went with the full package. The dress was beautiful, the photographs polished, and even people they had not seen in years gathered in one place.

After the ceremony, they checked the settlement and the remaining balance. Thirty-one million won, gone in a day. They both knew that money would have put Gangnam months closer.

The photographs arrived a few days later. Their parents and the two of them were smiling in the same frame. It had been an expensive day, and one they could never stage again.

title: Daeun's Side
description:
The wedding day. The groom's entrance was already over.

{name} had walked the aisle alone and taken his place at the altar. The rear doors were still closed. The first person he noticed was Daeun's mother, in the screen-left bride's front row, seated closest to the aisle.

A dusty-rose jeogori and deep raspberry chima. Her hands rested one over the other on her lap. Her body faced the altar, but her eyes never left the door her daughter would enter through. The guests behind her receded into dark outlines, leaving only the mother in warm color.

{name} recognized in her face the expression Daeun wore when she had been holding something in for too long: the mouth of someone trying not to cry.

choices.text: Follow her gaze to the doors that are still closed.
choices.result_text:
Without looking away from the doors, her mother let out one slow breath.

There was no impatience in the way she waited. It was the patience of someone who had always known her daughter would come out at her own pace.

{name} bowed once, then looked across to the groom's side.

description_if_known.daeun_hometown_visited:

{name} had walked the aisle alone and taken his place at the altar. Daeun's mother, up on the dawn bus from the countryside, sat closest to the aisle in the screen-left bride's front row.

On the dusty-rose jeogori and deep raspberry chima rested the same work-thickened hands he had seen at her table. Her body faced the altar, but her eyes never left the door her daughter would enter through. When her gaze briefly met {name}'s, she gave one silent nod, just as she had that night over dinner.

{name} recognized in her face the expression Daeun wore when she had been holding something in for too long: the mouth of someone trying not to cry.

title: The Groom's Side
description:
The screen-right groom's side was sparse. His father sat alone in the front-row seat closest to the aisle. The dark charcoal honju suit still seemed unfamiliar on him; his shoulders held a little too stiffly.

His body faced the altar, but his face and eyes had turned toward the door Daeun would enter through. Hands that had worked a factory floor for a lifetime lay neatly on his knees. Most of the chairs behind him were empty.

For five years, {name} had watched charts instead of meeting people and worked overtime instead of going out. Still, today, his father was keeping the seat he had promised to take.

choices.text: Don't avoid the empty groom's chairs. Look all the way down the rows.
choices.result_text:
He had thought that if he didn't look, it might not count. So {name} looked at the chairs one by one.

The seats were empty, but faces came to mind: people whose calls he had put off, people he hadn't met because the numbers came first, people he'd promised to call as one season passed into another.

His breath caught once. He did not look away.

choices.text: Turn to the bride's side and bow first to the people who came today.
choices.result_text:
When {name} bowed, quiet applause spread through the bride's side.

A mart coworker who had traded shifts, a hometown friend who had taken the dawn bus, relatives he'd met only once. Every one of them had made time to be here for Daeun.

In the front row, her mother brought her hands together and bowed back. Only then did {name} understand that this wedding was not something he was doing alone.

description_if_known.father_passed&hyunsu_reconnected:
The front-row seat closest to the aisle on the screen-right groom's side — the seat where his father should have been — stood empty. Hyunsu sat alone one row behind it.

Hyunsu pushed up his glasses, then looked not at {name} but toward the still-closed doors. Someone who knew these five years was here. The person he most wanted to show this moment was not.

{name} tried to smile, and his throat tightened. If money could have moved time forward, today he would have paid anything.
description_if_known.father_passed:
One front-row seat closest to the aisle on the screen-right groom's side stood out more sharply than all the other empty chairs. It was where his father should have been.

If only he had been a little faster, his father could have sat there and seen this. Not even money could move time forward today.

{name} looked at the empty chair back for a long time. No one sat there, yet the seat already belonged to someone.
description_if_known.father_reconciled&hyunsu_reconnected:
His father straightened in the front-row aisle seat on the screen-right groom's side. Hyunsu sat alone one row behind him. Both faces and both sets of eyes pointed toward the doors that were still closed.

His father, whose hands had worked a factory floor for a lifetime, and the friend who knew these five years had both come. Rows of empty chairs or not, those two reached him first.

Hyunsu pushed up his glasses and mouthed, "Hyung, look ahead. You'll ruin the photos."
description_if_known.hyunsu_reconnected:
The screen-right groom's side was sparse. His father sat in the front-row aisle seat; Hyunsu had come alone and sat one row behind him. Both watched the doors that were still closed.

Hyunsu had not come as someone's husband or father. He had come simply as Hyunsu, taking the seat he had promised to take.

Beyond the flowers, Hyunsu pushed up his glasses. {name} laughed, and his throat tightened.
description_if_known.father_reconciled:
The screen-right groom's side was sparse. Still, his father straightened in the front-row seat closest to the aisle. Hands that had worked a factory floor for a lifetime rested on his knees; his face and eyes turned toward the door Daeun would enter through.

Rows of empty chairs or not, his father had come. Today, that was bigger than a hundred guests.

{name} watched his father's profile, then turned toward the same doors.

title: At Daeun's Pace
description:
The music changed. "Please welcome the bride."

The rear doors opened and Daeun appeared. On her first step, the hem of her dress swept the aisle. On the second, a flash went off. On the third, applause and music folded into each other.

Even through the noise, he saw Daeun's lips move.

"Minjun."

She was too far away for him to hear her, but he could recognize his own name. Daeun did not hurry. As she had for five years, she was coming toward {name} at her own pace.

The distance between them shortened one step at a time.

choices.text: As if he heard his name, loosen his rigid shoulders and meet Daeun's eyes.
choices.result_text:
When their eyes met, Daeun's mouth softened.

The applause and camera shutters moved one step farther away. He saw, in order, her hands around the bouquet, the lips pressed together to hold back tears, the smile spreading at the corners of her eyes.

Only a few steps remained. The empty groom's section and the person approaching him now fit in the same view.

description_if_known.namsan_lock_daeun:
The music changed. "Please welcome the bride."

The rear doors opened and Daeun appeared. On her first step, the hem of her dress swept the aisle. On the second, a flash went off.

Beyond the path she was walking, he remembered the padlock they had fastened together on the Namsan railing. "Come find it in ten years." The promise from that night was now coming toward {name} down the aisle.

Through the noise, Daeun's lips moved. "Minjun." Even at that distance, he knew his own name. Daeun walked at her own pace, and the space between them shortened one step at a time.

title: Before She Reaches Him
description:
Daeun was halfway down the aisle.

On one side was Daeun coming closer: the person who had passed him triangle gimbap across a convenience-store counter, the person who had fallen asleep on his shoulder in that narrow room on a rainy night.

On the other were the empty chairs. The calls he had put off and the faces he'd lost while chasing Gangnam remained in the shape of neat chair backs.

Behind her bouquet, Daeun quietly formed the words, "It's okay." He couldn't tell whether she meant the empty seats, his shaking hands, or the last five years.

Before Daeun reached the altar, {name}'s gaze stood one last time between the two.

choices.text: Look only at Daeun. The groom's side is empty, but she's coming toward him.
choices.result_text:
Daeun walked down the aisle toward {name}. Instead of the empty seats beside him, {name} watched the person coming closer.

However many guests there were, it didn't matter. One person to spend a life with was enough.
Daeun stopped before the altar. The empty groom's section, strangely, no longer stung.

choices.text: Beyond Daeun approaching him, the empty groom's section stings. What did he run five years for?
choices.result_text:
From the altar, {name}'s eyes kept catching on the empty chairs.

Gangnam had come closer, and along that road people had dropped away one by one.
Only today could he see the tally. What he'd gained, and what he'd lost without even a goodbye.
The short time it took Daeun to reach him felt unusually long.
